item.title: BIS renews for one year the temporary denial order against URAL Airlines JSC (Russia)
item.description: BIS granted OEE's request to renew the temporary denial order (TDO) issued in this matter on September 30, 2025 against URAL Airlines JSC [FR Doc. 2026-19927, preamble]. OEE submitted the written renewal request on August 13, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section I]. The renewal runs for one year [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV]. Section II.A states that in cases demonstrating a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations, BIS may request renewal for an additional period not exceeding one year [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.A]. Footnote 3 in Section I states that, at the time of the earlier renewal, Section 766.24(d) provided for additional 180-day renewal periods [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section I, n.3]. The Assistant Secretary found that Ural violated the Regulations and the TDO, that the violations were significant and deliberate, and that there is a likelihood of imminent violations [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section III]. The extended period rests on a finding that Ural engaged in a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations of the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section III]. BIS's evidence lists flights dated June 25, 2026 to August 26, 2026 by three aircraft (serial numbers 05055, 02343 and 07206; types A320-232 and A321-231) into and out of Russia from/to Sukhumi, Dushanbe, Khujand and Kulob, and domestically within Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B, table]. The table includes flight dates of August 17, 2026 and August 26, 2026, which are later than the August 13, 2026 request date, and the source does not explain this [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B, table]. The order is dated September 24, 2026 and is effective immediately [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV].

item.title: BIS renews Azur Air temporary denial order for one year (Russia aviation, ECCN 9A991)
item.description: BIS granted the Office of Export Enforcement's request to renew the temporary denial order issued on September 16, 2025 against Azur Air [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Preamble]. The renewal runs for one year [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV]. OEE submitted its written renewal request on August 3, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order states that, given the temporary suspension of international mail service to Russia, OEE attempted to deliver the request to Azur by alternative means, and that no opposition to the renewal was received [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order records the TDO history as an initial 180-day order signed April 7, 2022, renewed on October 3, 2022, March 29, 2023, September 23, 2023, September 20, 2024 and September 16, 2025 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order states that this renewal reflects a corrected address for Azur, which was introduced by a modification of the September 20, 2024 renewal order dated January 31, 2025 in the text (footnote 5 refers to a January 30, 2025 modification order) [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The Assistant Secretary found that BIS's evidence convincingly demonstrates that Azur violated the Regulations and the TDO, that the violations were significant and deliberate, and that there is a likelihood of imminent violations [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section III]. The order bases the one-year period on a finding that Azur engaged in a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations of the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section III]. The order's table lists flights dated March 9, 2026 to July 17, 2026 by Boeing 757 aircraft (tail numbers RA-73071, RA-73029, RA-73076 and RA-73072) between Russia and Turkey, Vietnam or Thailand, and within Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section II.B]. The order is dated September 11, 2026 and is effective immediately [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV].

item.title: BIS renews one-year Temporary Denial Order against PJSC Aeroflot for continued EAR violations
item.description: BIS renewed, for a period of one year, the Temporary Denial Order (TDO) originally issued against PJSC Aeroflot on April 7, 2022, based on evidence that Aeroflot continued to operate aircraft subject to the EAR and classified under ECCN 9A991.b on flights into, out of, and within Russia through July 2026, in violation of the September 19, 2025 renewal order and/or the Regulations [FR Doc. 2026-19020, Section II.B]. The Assistant Secretary found the violations 'significant and deliberate' and part of 'a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations,' justifying renewal for an extended one-year period [FR Doc. 2026-19020, Section III].

item.title: BIS renews one-year Temporary Denial Order against UTair Aviation JSC for continued EAR violations
item.description: BIS renewed, for a period of one year, the Temporary Denial Order (TDO) originally issued April 7, 2022 and previously renewed on October 3, 2022, March 29, 2023, September 23, 2023, September 20, 2024, and September 16, 2025 against UTair Aviation JSC, based on evidence that UTair continued to operate aircraft classified under ECCN 9A991.b on flights into, out of, and within Russia without required BIS authorization, in violation of the Regulations and the prior TDO [FR Doc. 2026-19019, Section II.B]. The Assistant Secretary found the violations significant and deliberate and part of a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations, warranting renewal for the maximum one-year period under 15 CFR 766.24(d) [FR Doc. 2026-19019, Section III].

item.title: Commission adopts 2026 update of EU dual-use control list (Annex I, Reg. 2021/821); not yet in force
item.description: On 14 September 2026 the European Commission adopted a Delegated Regulation updating the EU dual-use export control list in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 [C(2026)6323]. The announcement states that the update aligns the list with 2025 decisions of the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group and the Nuclear Suppliers Group, and includes commitments Member States accepted as Wassenaar members to control additional items uniformly [C(2026)6323]. The announcement states that the update adds new dual-use items, including semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment and materials, advanced computing integrated circuits and electronic assemblies such as ICs incorporating one or multiple Digital Processing Units, ceramic matrix composites reinforced with mullite, inductive-sensing rotary encoders, additive manufacturing equipment for energetic materials, chemical vapour deposition equipment for silicon carbide fibres, and technology for the development of axial compressors of gas turbine engines [C(2026)6323]. The semiconductor examples given are atomic layer deposition equipment for molybdenum and ruthenium, equipment for the development and inspection of Extreme Ultra-Violet masks and reticles, and single wafer cleaning equipment [C(2026)6323]. The announcement also states that certain control parameters are modified and certain technical definitions and descriptions are updated [C(2026)6323]. The act was adopted by the Commission and is not yet published in the Official Journal or in force; it enters into force upon publication in the Official Journal after the usual two-month scrutiny period for the Council and the European Parliament [C(2026)6323].

item.title: State Dept imposes INKSNA nonproliferation measures, incl. procurement ban, on 22 foreign persons
item.description: The Department of State determined that a number of foreign persons engaged in activities warranting measures under section 3 of the Iran, North Korea, and Syria Nonproliferation Act (INKSNA); these measures went into effect July 24, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-15759, DATES]. The measures bar U.S. government procurement from and assistance to the listed persons, terminate USML sales and existing Arms Export Control Act sales/services, and bar new individual licenses (with suspension of existing licenses) for items controlled under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 or the Export Administration Regulations, for two years from the effective date unless the Secretary of State determines otherwise [FR Doc. 2026-15759, Supplementary Information].

item.title: BIS moves firearm sound suppressors from ITAR to EAR, adds new ECCNs and TMP tools-of-trade exception
item.description: BIS revised the EAR and CCL to control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors that are being removed from the USML by a companion State Department IFR, creating new item paragraphs 0A501.f (suppressors usable with rifles/pistols under 0A501, 0A506, 0A507, or interchangeably with shotguns) and 0A502.f (suppressors for exclusive use with shotguns under 0A502/0A508) [FR Doc. 2026-14942, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION, Section I.B]. New reasons for control (NS1/RS1/FC1/UN/AT1 for 0A501.f; FC1/UN/AT1 plus a new RS control for 0A502.f) and license exception eligibility (LVS, BAG, STA, TMP) were added for the new paragraphs [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.C-D]. BIS also revised License Exception TMP (Sec. 740.9) to add a new paragraph (a)(2) authorizing temporary export/reexport of firearms and related items, including suppressors, as 'tools of trade' without a license, subject to quantity limits and effective-control/return conditions [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section II]. Sec. 758.10 entry-clearance requirements for temporary imports were broadened from listed end-item ECCNs to all 0x5zz and certain '600 series' items subject to the EAR that are also on the USMIL [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section III].

Additions under IRAN-EO13902 include LAVASANI, Ahmad Navai [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57949], CDM TRADING LIMITED [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57934], ABADI, Shokufeh Rostam [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57945], MOHSEN KHANDAN AND PARTNERS GENERAL PARTNERSHIP COMPANY [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57933], KHANDAN, Mohsen [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57942], KHANDAN, Ali Asghar [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57943], DARBANI, Mohammad [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57947], LAVASANI AND PARTNERS GENERAL PARTNERSHIP COMPANY [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57948], LAVASANI, Amir Navai [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57950], SARSHARI, Zahra [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57946], and MOHAMMAD DARBANI AND PARTNERS EXCHANGE GENERAL PARTNERSHIP COMPANY [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57944]. One individual, ANSARI, Ali, was added under programmes IRAN-EO13876, SDGT, IFSR, and IRGC [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57957]. SMART GLOBAL LIMITED was added under IRAN-EO13876 and SDGT [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57960]. Additions under CUBA-EO14404 include GRUPO EMPRESARIAL DEL COMERCIO EXTERIOR [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58051], CORPORACION ANTILLANA EXPORTADORA SA [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58056], COREYDAN S.A. [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58057], GRUPO EMPRESARIAL DE TRANSPORTE MARITIMO PORTUARIO [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58054], ENETEC S.A. [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58052], ORGANIZACION SUPERIOR DE DIRECCION EMPRESARIAL CAUDAL S.A. [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58053], ASSOCIATION OF COMBATANTS OF THE CUBAN REVOLUTION [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58046], MINISTRY OF TOURISM OF CUBA [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58059], RAPID RESPONSE BRIGADES [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58058], and MILICIAS DE TROPAS TERRITORIALES [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:58055]. Two additions under CYBER4 are FIRST VPN SERVICE [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57975] and RASHEVSKYI, Dmytro [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:57978]. Two further added entries are present in the full event record but were truncated from this digest [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:snap-7e70fdca5d98945e]. A total of 1,730 existing SDN entries were modified; the sole field changed in all modified records is 'ids', indicating internal identifier updates with no change to designated names, programmes, or other substantive fields [CSL:Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) - Treasury Department:snap-7e70fdca5d98945e].

item.title: BIS extends ECCN 3A090.a approved IC designer application deadline from April 13, 2026 to December 31, 2026
item.description: BIS has amended Note 1 to ECCN 3A090.a in paragraphs a.(2) and (3) by removing the date 'April 13, 2026' wherever it occurs and replacing it with 'December 31, 2026' [FR Doc. 2026-06851, Supplement No. 1 to Part 774, ECCN 3A090 amendment]. The triggering date for authorized IC designer status and the submission deadline for applications to become an approved IC designer are both extended by approximately eight months [FR Doc. 2026-06851, SUMMARY]. Applicants who submit by December 31, 2026 may be considered authorized IC designers for 180 days after that date [FR Doc. 2026-06851, DATES]. BIS estimates the extension will result in approximately 20 additional approved IC designers and an increase of 385 burden hours under OMB Control Number 0694-0137 [FR Doc. 2026-06851, Rulemaking Requirements §2]. BIS also estimates approximately 75 additional advisory opinions and 38 additional burden hours under OMB Control Number 0694-0088 [FR Doc. 2026-06851, Rulemaking Requirements §2].

item.title: Corrigendum deletes the sub-193 nm light-source criterion from Annex I entry 3B501.f.1.a
item.description: The corrigendum of 9 February 2026 to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2003 replaces the text of entry 3B501.f.1.a, 'A light source wavelength shorter than 193 nm; or', with 'Not used;' [OJ L 2026/90092, entry 3B501.f.1.a]. 'Not used' is the Annex I placeholder for a deleted provision: the sub-193 nm light-source criterion no longer exists as a route into entry 3B501.f.1, whose remaining sub-points are unchanged [OJ L 2026/90092, entry 3B501.f.1.a].
